text:
Coverage, with real numbers.
For a four hundred sixty megahertz repeater on a hundred fifty-foot tower over suburban ground, the Okumura-Hata model gives about one hundred forty-six decibels of loss at eight miles.
With fifty dB m of power out, a portable radio gets about minus ninety-six dB m there, well above its minus one hundred nineteen sensitivity.

Measure the room plays a test sweep through the speakers, and works out the reverberation time by octave and the speech transmission index.
A classroom with about one second of reverberation and a quiet background comes out around zero point five eight, which passes the [NFPA](/ˌɛnˌɛfpˌiˈA/) seventy-two target of zero point five.
